items.title: Amazon ECS now supports GPU sharing with NVIDIA Multi-Process Service (MPS)
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now supports GPU sharing with NVIDIA Multi-Process Service (MPS), enabling you to run multiple Amazon ECS tasks concurrently on a single NVIDIA GPU. GPU sharing helps you increase GPU utilization and reduce infrastructure costs for workloads that use only part of a GPU's capacity, such as small-model inference, AV/ADAS simulations, embedding generation, and multi-model serving.

With GPU sharing, you can pack more workloads onto each GPU instance without changing your application code. You define the GPU memory each container needs and can optionally set a maximum share of GPU compute, and Amazon ECS places tasks on GPUs with available capacity as your services scale and deploy. GPU sharing is supported on Amazon ECS Managed Instances and Amazon ECS on Amazon EC2. On Amazon ECS Managed Instances, Amazon ECS also monitors the MPS control daemon that enables sharing on each instance. If the daemon stops or becomes unhealthy, Amazon ECS automatically replaces the instance and moves your tasks to healthy capacity, so your GPU workloads keep running without manual intervention.

To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, AWS CloudFormation, or other infrastructure-as-code tools to create a capacity provider with NVIDIA GPU instances, set the GPU sharing strategy and memory in the container definition of your task definition, and create a service on that capacity provider. This capability is available in all AWS commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, visit the Amazon ECS GPU sharing documentation.

items.title: SageMaker MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker AI MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16, bringing a redesigned tracing experience and faster experiment tracking to your generative AI and machine learning workflows.

MLflow 3.16 improves debugging and analysis of generative AI applications and agents. The redesigned trace explorer is now the default, with adjustable row height, reorderable columns, custom columns from any trace tag or metadata field. This release also accelerates metric charts for experiments with large metric histories.

New MLflow Apps are created on MLflow 3.16 by default. Existing MLflow Apps will be upgraded to MLflow 3.16 during an upcoming maintenance window, with no action required.

MLflow 3.16 is available in all AWS Regions where MLflow Apps are available. To learn more, visit the SageMaker AI MLflow developer guide.

items.title: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports up to 384 ACUs
items.summary:
Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. Each ACU provides approximately 2 gibibytes (GiB) of memory with corresponding CPU and networking, so a single Aurora serverless database can now scale up to 768 GiB of memory. When the workload completes, Aurora serverless automatically scales down to zero. This makes Aurora serverless especially well-suited for agentic AI applications, which typically have bursts of activity, long idle windows, and unpredictable traffic patterns. Aurora serverless handles all of it automatically, scaling capacity with your agents, so you only pay for what you use.

With 384 ACU support, customers can now use Aurora serverless for even more demanding workloads while continuing to scale down to zero when not in use, paying only for the capacity consumed. For new clusters, select a supported Aurora PostgreSQL engine version and set your maximum capacity up to 384 ACUs. For existing clusters on Platform Version 4, simply modify the cluster to update the maximum capacity setting (and the engine version if needed). There will be no downtime if your database is already on Platform Version 4. For existing clusters on older platform versions, upgrade to Platform Version 4 through a pending maintenance action. 384 ACU support is available for Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23, running on Platform Version 4.

To learn more, see Aurora serverless capacity in the Amazon Aurora User Guide. For pricing details and Region availability, visit Amazon Aurora Pricing.  To get started, create or modify an Aurora serverless database in the AWS Management Console.

items.title: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now supports changing durability on existing clusters
items.summary:
Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you enable or disable durability on your existing node-based clusters without creating a new cluster. Previously, you couldn't change the durability configuration of an existing cluster in place. This made it harder to move from caching to persistent data store use cases, or to adapt as your application requirements change. Now you can change durability at any point in your application's lifecycle.

You can choose between two durability options: synchronous and asynchronous writes. Synchronous writes persist data across at least two AZs before responding to the client, designed for zero data loss at single-digit millisecond write latency. Asynchronous writes persist data after responding to the client, maintaining microsecond write latency at no additional cost. However, up to 10 seconds of uncommitted data could be lost in the rare event of a failure. Both options maintain microsecond read latency. You can now use ElastiCache for a broader set of use cases beyond caching where data loss is unacceptable such as AI agent long-term memory, AI agent workflow state, knowledge bases for RAG applications, payment tokenization, and real-time inventory management.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where ElastiCache for Valkey 9.0 and later is available. To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS SDK, or AWS CLI. For pricing, see the  Amazon ElastiCache pricing page . To learn more, see  Durability  in the ElastiCache documentation.

items.title: Amazon Corretto October 2026 Patch Updates
items.summary:
On October 26, 2026 Amazon announced a patch update for the following Amazon Corretto Long-Term Support (LTS) and Feature Release (FR) versions of OpenJDK. Corretto 27.0.1.0.11, 25.0.5.0.10, 21.0.13.0.11, 17.0.21.0.11, 11.0.33.0.10, and 8u512 are now available for download. Amazon Corretto is a no-cost, multi-platform, production-ready distribution of OpenJDK.

Visit the Corretto home page to download Corretto 27, Corretto 25, Corretto 21, Corretto 17, Corretto 11, or Corretto 8. You can also get the updates on your Linux system by configuring a Corretto Apt, Yum, or Apk repo.

Feedback is welcomed!

items.title: Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill for existing container images
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replication backfill, enabling you to replicate existing images in your private registry to your configured replication registry destinations. Previously, replication only applied to images pushed after the replication configuration was enabled, requiring customers to manually retag images to trigger replication of preexisting images. With replication backfill, you can now replicate your full image catalog to new or existing destinations with a single API call.

Replication backfill is useful when expanding to a new AWS Region, validating disaster recovery readiness, updating replication rules, or ensuring complete image catalogs exist across Regions for compliance purposes. You can run up to ten backfill jobs concurrently, monitor progress and per-image results through new APIs, and stop a job at any time without deleting images that have already been replicated.

Replication backfill is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECR is available. To learn more, refer to the Amazon ECR user guide.

items.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces the general availability of OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra on Amazon Bedrock. GPT-6.1 Terra expands the GPT-6 family with a balance of capability, speed, and cost efficiency for everyday workloads. 

As the newest model in the Terra line, GPT-6.1 Terra combines detailed visual reasoning, accurate computer use, and improved factuality and natural writing over GPT-5.6 Terra, for complex workflows. In OpenAI’s Agents’ Last Exam evaluation, it scored 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra, performed on par with GPT-6 Astra, and completed tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. GPT-6.1 Terra offers balanced performance with input and output token prices at least 50% lower than those of GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra. It supports a context window of up to 1 million input tokens and accepts both text and image inputs. The Amazon Bedrock inference engine delivers the performance, security, and scale required for enterprise workloads. 

You can call GPT-6.1 Terra directly through Amazon Bedrock APIs or configure ChatGPT Work and Codex to use the model on Amazon Bedrock. Use it to draft proposals, interpret technical drawings, investigate codebases, and build agents that operate across business systems.  Established AWS controls help you secure workloads, govern access, and audit model invocation activity. 

You can get started in the Amazon Bedrock console or programmatically through supported Amazon Bedrock APIs. For information about supported AWS Regions, endpoints, APIs, features, inference profiles and pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation.

items.title: Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports ModifyVolume API
items.summary:
Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports the ModifyVolume API, which lets you change volume size, volume type, IOPS, or throughput in place, without detaching the volume or restarting the instance. Previously, changing storage capacity or performance on a deployed managed instance required rebuilding it.

With ModifyVolume, you can increase volume size up to 16,384 GiB, switch between supported Amazon EBS volume types, adjust IOPS for gp3, io1, and io2 volumes, and modify throughput for gp3 volumes. The API supports idempotency tokens to prevent duplicate changes, and you can track progress with the Amazon EC2 DescribeVolumesModifications operation.

ModifyVolume is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances is available.

To get started, call ModifyVolume directly, or use it through your WorkSpaces Core partner solution once available. To learn more, see ModifyVolume in the WorkSpaces Instances API Reference and Limitations in the Amazon EBS User Guide, or visit WorkSpaces Core.

items.title: Amazon IVS Low-Latency Streaming now provides a failover slate
items.summary:
Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Low-Latency Streaming now provides a failover slate, an animated image that IVS displays to viewers when a broadcaster's stream is unexpectedly interrupted. Instead of a buffering wheel or frozen frame, viewers see the slate until the broadcaster reconnects. Live playback then resumes automatically, without viewers needing to refresh their player.

The failover slate helps you retain your audience during momentary disruptions and is ideal for broadcasters streaming from mobile devices or from locations with unreliable connectivity. You can enable the failover slate on new or existing channels and monitor slate activity with Amazon EventBridge events and Amazon CloudWatch metrics.

Amazon IVS is a managed live streaming solution designed to make low-latency or real-time video available to viewers around the world. Visit the AWS Region table for a full list of AWS Regions where the Amazon IVS console and APIs for control and creation of video streams are available.

To learn more, see the Amazon IVS Failover Slate documentation.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio adds light mode support for IDC-based domains
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces light mode support in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio for Identity Center (IDC) based domains. Customers can now configure the visual interface mode to match their preference, choosing between dark and light themes. With this launch, customers can set this visual preference in both IAM-based and IDC-based domains. 

Light mode helps improve readability in bright environments and provides a familiar visual experience for customers who prefer lighter interfaces. Combined with the existing dark mode, this update gives you full control over the appearance of your development environment, improving accessibility and reducing eye strain across varying lighting conditions. In SageMaker Unified Studio settings, you can choose 'Customize appearance' under your Profile settings to select between visual modes including dark mode, light mode, and device setting, which matches your operating system's setting. The setting persists across browsers and devices.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, see the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio User Guide.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer expands testing and simulation to validate flow action outcomes
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to validate the outcomes of your customer experience flow actions during testing and simulation. In addition to confirming that an action started, you can now verify the data it returns when it completes, such as a Lambda function response, an Amazon Lex resolved intent, or the variables set by an Agentic CX block. When a test fails, you can pinpoint the exact action that returned an unexpected result instead of tracing it back from a downstream step, so you can resolve issues faster and launch flow changes with greater confidence.

To learn more about this feature, see testing and simulation in the Connect Customer administrator guide. For a complete list of testing and simulation capabilities available by AWS Region, refer to Availability of Connect Customer features by Region. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you view metrics by customer lifetime value and repeat-caller status
items.summary: Now you can view your metrics across customer segments: customer lifetime value (LTV) and repeat callers. See how any metric differs for repeat callers versus the rest of your contacts, or how results hold up among your highest-LTV customers; so you can spot the groups trending the wrong way before it shows up in the aggregate. Where a segment is underperforming, you can act. Route high-LTV customers to your most effective people, adjust the knowledge bases and self-service flows that repeat callers are falling back from, or refine agent guidance for segments where satisfaction is slipping. The segment tells you where to look; the metrics tell you what to fix.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now measures the outcomes that drive retention and revenue
items.summary: Amazon Connect Customer now scores the outcome of your customer interactions. It shows whether the customer left satisfied, is at risk of churning, made a purchase, or resolved their need in self-service. You can now see whether an interaction worked, not just how efficiently it ran. Each metric comes with a default definition you can adjust to match how your business defines success and are available both through the analytics dashboards and APIs.

items.title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports cross-Region trusted identity propagation
items.summary:
Trusted identity propagation carries a user's identity with their request, so AWS services can grant permissions based on who the user is and their underlying group associations, and log that user's access for auditing. With cross-Region support, this identity context can now be propagated to AWS services running in different AWS Regions, giving you greater flexibility in how you architect and deploy across AWS Regions.

Customers often distribute workloads across AWS Regions for many reasons including separating the compute from the data it queries, to running workloads where capacity is available, or for disaster recovery and global scale. Previously, trusted identity propagation required all of the AWS services accessing a user's identity to reside in the same AWS Region. To reach services in another AWS Region, customers had to either grant access through broad IAM roles that cannot distinguish individual users or consolidate all their services into a single AWS Region. With cross-Region trusted identity propagation, a user's identity travels with the request across AWS Regions automatically, so you can grant access based on who the user is and their underlying group associations, and audit who accessed which resources, while preserving fine-grained access control for every individual user.

Cross-Region trusted identity propagation is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. For the list of Regions where IAM Identity Center is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region.  For more information, see Trusted identity propagation in the IAM Identity Center User Guide.

items.title: AWS Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation
items.summary:
AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now supports Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), a post-quantum cryptography standard under NIST FIPS 203, which enables two parties to establish a shared secret. NIST designed ML-KEM to replace the classical key-establishment schemes, like DH/ECDH key agreement, and RSA-based key transport, in their strategic cryptographic roadmap (see NIST IR 8547). ML-KEM addresses the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat to those classical schemes, where an adversary records the key-establishment exchange today and recovers the shared secret once sufficiently powerful quantum computers become available.

KMS supports all three ML-KEM key specs defined in NIST FIPS 203: ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024. The Encapsulate API uses the public key to produce a random 32-byte shared secret and its ciphertext form. The Decapsulate API recovers the shared secret from ciphertext using the corresponding private key. KMS protects the private key of an ML-KEM key pair in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated hardware security modules (HSMs). You can use the GetPublicKey API to export the public key and distribute it to partners, client applications, or external systems for performing the encapsulate operation locally using cryptographic libraries like AWS-LC, OpenSSL, or Bouncy Castle.

ML-KEM is available in all AWS Regions where KMS is available, except the the Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain), and China Regions. For more information, see Key spec reference in the AWS KMS Developer Guide.

items.title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now supports Launch Before Terminate at account-level to replace instances
items.summary:
AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now lets you enable Launch Before Terminate as the default replacement behavior across all Auto Scaling groups in your account. When enabled, Auto Scaling launches a replacement instance and waits for it to pass health checks before terminating the instance it replaces, helping your applications maintain full capacity and availability during instance replacement events. This applies to replacement events such as instance refreshes, rebalancing, health checks, and maximum-instance-lifetime replacements.

You can enable Launch Before Terminate through AWS EC2 Auto Scaling account settings, which let you configure the behavior once at the account level instead of on each Auto Scaling group individually. You can manage the setting with the new `PutAccountSetting` and `DescribeAccountSettings` APIs, available through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs.

Launch Before Terminate is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost.

To learn more, see Launch Before Terminate in the AWS EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide and AWS EC2 Auto Scaling API Reference Guide.

items.title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports endpoint connection management
items.summary:
AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports managing external connections through a new endpoint registry. The registry provides a centralized interface to register and manage both standard endpoints—devices or software outside the service, such as cameras, sources, monitors, and other destinations—and connections to other AWS accounts. You can share registered endpoints directly with other AWS accounts, streamlining cross-account live video workflows. 

Cross-account endpoint sharing lowers costs by reducing required compute instances and decreases latency through fewer network hops when sharing live content across AWS accounts.. It also eliminates the need to manually chain router inputs and outputs, coordinate IP addresses out of band, and manage connection security. The endpoint registry gives you a single interface to manage all external connections to MediaConnect for seamless integration with your existing infrastructure. You get cross-account sharing through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), transparent verification of encryption and protocol controls, and built-in connection management with Connection Manager. Use cases include content distributors sharing live feeds with downstream partners, broadcasters collaborating across organizational boundaries, and media workflows that require secure cross-account video transport.

MediaConnect endpoint registry is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router is available, at no additional cost. For more information, see the AWS Elemental MediaConnect User Guide.

items.title: Amazon RDS now supports the latest Cumulative Update and GDR updates for Microsoft SQL Server
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports the latest Cumulative Updates (CU) and General Distribution Release (GDR) updates for Microsoft SQL Server. This release includes support for Microsoft SQL Server 2017 CU31+GDR KB5122774 (RDS version 14.00.3550.4.v1), SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR KB5122772 (RDS version 15.00.4490.9.v1), SQL Server 2022 CU27 KB5104824 (RDS version 16.00.4295.3.v1) and SQL Server 2025 CU9 KB5122048 (RDS version 17.00.5005.3.v1).

For additional information on the improvements and fixes included in these updates, see Microsoft documentation for KB5122774, KB5122772, KB5104824 and KB5122048. We recommend that you upgrade your Amazon RDS for SQL Server instances to apply these updates using Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. You can learn more about upgrading your database instance in the Amazon RDS SQL Server User Guide for upgrading your RDS Microsoft SQL Server DB engine.

items.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports OAuth for Apache Iceberg REST Catalog APIs
items.summary:
AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports OAuth 2.0 bearer token authentication for Apache Iceberg REST Catalog (IRC) APIs using AWS Sign-In. The Apache Iceberg REST Catalog specification defines OAuth 2.0 as its standard authentication mechanism, and query engines such as Apache Spark, Trino, and Apache Flink implement it natively. These engines and external integration partners can now authenticate to the Glue Data Catalog Iceberg endpoint using standard OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, in addition to AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4).

You can now grant partners federated access to your Iceberg tables without distributing AWS credentials. Using OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), you exchange an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity token for a short-lived, Glue-scoped bearer token and include it in IRC requests following the same standards-based pattern used across the Iceberg ecosystem. Access remains governed by AWS IAM and AWS Lake Formation permissions. Common use cases include enabling third-party analytics and data cloud platforms to query tables in the Glue Data Catalog through a single, consistent authentication path.

This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Glue and Lake Formation are available. To learn more, see the AWS Glue User Guide and AWS Sign-In User Guide.

items.title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports domain filtering and user location controls
items.summary:
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports two new controls that give you more precision over the results that ground a model's response: domain filtering and user location. Both are configured directly on the web_search tool in your existing OpenAI Responses API request.

With domain filtering, you can restrict Web Search results to a set of domains you choose. Using the filters parameter, you specify up to 100 allowed_domains to limit results to trusted sources, or up to 100 blocked_domains to exclude sources you don't want. This is useful when you want responses grounded only in specific sites, or when you need to keep certain domains out of results.

With user location, you can optionally specify location parameters so that Web Search can return results relevant to that geography. This helps with location-dependent questions, such as regional availability or local services.

Domain filtering and user location are available in all AWS Regions where Web Search is supported: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). To get started, see the Web Search section in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. For pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock pricing page.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now supports persistent chat across linked AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides customers a mechanism to deliver long, persistent chat experiences across linked AWS Regions. With this capability, end users can resume previous conversations with full context, metadata, and transcripts carried over across Regions, eliminating the need for end users to repeat information and allowing agents to provide personalized service with access to the entire conversation history across AWS Regions.

For example, an end user can start a chat in US-East (N. Virginia) and later come back to it in the linked US-West (Oregon) Region, continuing the same conversation with an agent with full conversation history and chat attachment. To adopt this capability, onboard to Global routing.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency is supported. To learn more, visit Amazon Connect Customer Admin Guide.

items.title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now support 1:1 NAT
items.summary:
AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now provide managed one-to-one network address translation (NAT) directly on their attachments, through integration with Regional Private NAT Gateway. This enables customers to connect private networks that share the same IP address ranges without renumbering either network, deploying a NAT appliance, or writing return-traffic rules.

Networks with overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks have long been unable to communicate, a common blocker during mergers and acquisitions, when connecting partner networks over AWS Site-to-Site VPN, in multicloud connectivity, and when independently provisioned VPCs need to interconnect. Using this capability, customers can define address-translation rules on a AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN attachment, specifying the private IP range each source CIDR translates to, across Amazon VPC, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and SD-WAN appliances connected through Transit Gateway Connect. Both services apply translation automatically in both directions, with no separate return-traffic rule and no NAT appliance to deploy. AWS operates, scales, and manages the NAT capability as part of the attachment. For example, if a customer acquires a business and both VPCs use 10.0.0.0/16, they translate one VPC's addresses to a non-overlapping range on its attachment and connect the networks immediately. Customers set it up in minutes using the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), AWS SDKs, and AWS CloudFormation, and monitor translated traffic through Amazon CloudWatch metrics and Amazon EventBridge events.

AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN offer 1:1 NAT through Regional Private NAT Gateway in all AWS commercial regions where they operate. For full pricing details, see  Amazon VPC pricing . To learn more, see the  AWS Transit Gateway  and  AWS Cloud WAN  product pages, and the AWS Transit Gateway  and AWS Cloud WAN  documentation.

items.title: Amazon Corretto October 2026 Quarterly Updates
items.summary:
On October 22, 2026 Amazon announced quarterly security and critical updates for Amazon Corretto Long-Term Supported (LTS) versions of OpenJDK. Corretto 27.0.1.0.10, 25.0.5.0.9, 21.0.13.0.10, 17.0.21.0.10, 11.0.33.0.9, and 8u512 are now available for download. Amazon Corretto is a no-cost, multi-platform, production-ready distribution of OpenJDK.

Visit the Corretto home page to download Corretto 27, Corretto 25, Corretto 21, Corretto 17, Corretto 11, or Corretto 8. You can also get the updates on your Linux system by configuring a Corretto Apt, Yum, or Apk repo.

Feedback is welcomed!

items.title: Amazon MWAA now available in Mexico (Central) Region
items.summary:
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) Provisioned environments are now available in the Mexico (Central) Region (mx-central-1). Amazon MWAA Serverless was already available in this Region, and customers can now also use Amazon MWAA Provisioned environments for their Apache Airflow workflows. Amazon MWAA is a managed orchestration service for Apache Airflow that makes it easier for customers to set up and operate end-to-end data pipelines in the cloud at scale.

Customers can create Amazon MWAA Provisioned environments using the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, the AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. Customers in Mexico (Central) can now run their Amazon MWAA Provisioned workflows closer to their data sources and end users, reducing latency and helping meet data residency requirements. To learn more, visit the Amazon MWAA product page and the Amazon MWAA supported Regions documentation.

items.title: Amazon EMR on EKS reduces EMR charge by 30 percent
items.summary:
Amazon EMR announces a reduction of 30 percent in the EMR charge added to EKS when running EMR on EKS. This price decrease applies to both the per-vCPU-hour charge and the per-GB-hour charge, while the underlying Amazon EKS charges remain unchanged. All EMR workloads running on the EKS deployment option benefit from this change. Now, you can run Apache Spark workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) at a lower cost, and the new price automatically applies to your EMR on EKS workloads with no additional action required on your end.

The 30% reduction in EMR on EKS pricing is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon EMR on EKS is available. To learn more about EMR on EKS, visit the Amazon EMR on EKS documentation and the Amazon EMR pricing page.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports customizing the Customer Profiles app on the agent workspace
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer Profiles now allows administrators to customize which customer data that agents see in the agent workspace, and how it is displayed, using layouts they build in Profile Explorer. Customer Profiles provides agents with a real-time, unified view of each customer during interactions, combining contact history with customer data from multiple sources. Agents who handle different kinds of requests need different customer data in front of them.

Within Profile Explorer, administrators can create and save each layout of Customer Profiles widgets, such as contact history, contact information, and lifetime value calculated attributes, and assign it to agents in place of the legacy Customer Profiles view. For example, an airline baggage claims agent sees contact history, active flights, and baggage ticket information, while a loyalty agent sees loyalty status, preferences, and upcoming flights. Layouts can also include an AI Profile Summary that focuses the agent's attention on key customer insights by summarizing the customer profile.

You can use Profile Explorer in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London).

To learn more about Profile Explorer, see Profile Explorer in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

items.title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces the general availability of AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities. Continuum for code vulnerabilities discovers, validates, prioritizes, and remediates code vulnerabilities at machine speed.

Continuum for code vulnerabilities builds a context graph from your AWS environment, including resource topology, identity relationships, and network reachability. It knows which resources are part of your application, and which findings carry real business risk. It ingests your existing vulnerability findings, scans your code, and then confirms which findings are exploitable by testing them in an isolated sandbox. The findings are prioritized by business impact. And finally, it provides remediation patches as pull requests directly to developer workflows with exploitability proof and blast radius assessment attached.

Continuum for code vulnerabilities picks the right AI model for each task. Continuum starts in Learn mode where it proposes the remediation fixes that you approve. When it builds sufficient trust in its precision, you switch to the Enforce mode and let it act autonomous within the guardrails you set. 

AWS Continuum works alongside your existing AWS security services, including Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub. For more information about the AWS Regions where AWS Continuum is available, see the AWS Region table. To learn more, see the AWS Continuum product page.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service introduces intelligent ingestion for logs and documents in Amazon S3
items.summary:
Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now offers intelligent ingestion, a fully managed feature that turns logs and documents stored in Amazon S3 into searchable content in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (NextGen) collections . With intelligent ingestion, you can set up ingestion with a few clicks in the AWS Management Console or a single API call, with no ingestion infrastructure to manage. Intelligent ingestion supports observability logs and structured data in JSON, NDJSON, and JSON array formats, and unstructured files in PDF, Word, plain text, and Markdown formats.

You choose an S3 source and a collection index, and intelligent ingestion handles the rest. It automatically detects data types, parses documents, describes images, chunks text, generates vector embeddings, and indexes the results. You don't need to manage ingestion or document-processing infrastructure, or size capacity in advance. Use ingestion jobs for one-time loads such as migrations and backfills, or ingestion streams to keep an index in sync as new objects arrive in your bucket. Capacity scales with your workload up to the collection's configured limit, and you pay only for active processing. Source S3 buckets can be in the same AWS account as the collection or in a different account.

For logs and structured data, intelligent ingestion applies transformations and optionally adds embeddings, with no pipeline code. For unstructured data, it parses PDF, Word, plain text, and Markdown files while keeping headings, reading order, and tables intact, so the content lands in an index ready for semantic and hybrid search. When documents contain charts, diagrams, screenshots, or photos, a vision-language model generates text descriptions that are indexed with the surrounding content, making visual information searchable too.

Intelligent ingestion is available today for Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (NextGen) collections, with Amazon S3 as the source, in seven AWS Regions. To get started, open the Amazon OpenSearch Service console, choose your collection, and select the Ingestion tab. To learn more, see Intelligent ingestion in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide. For pricing, see Amazon OpenSearch Service pricing.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports a 5-second default refresh interval
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless reduces the default refresh interval to 5 seconds for both search and vector collections. The refresh interval controls how quickly newly ingested documents become available for search. By lowering the default from 10 seconds to 5 seconds, newly written data becomes searchable faster, giving applications quicker read-after-write visibility automatically, with no configuration changes and no action required on your part.

This improvement applies to the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless and takes effect by default on both search and vector collections. Faster refresh is valuable for workloads that continuously ingest data and need near real-time retrieval, including full-text search over frequently updated content as well as vector use cases such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, and recommendation and personalization systems. This means applications and AI agents can retrieve and act on the most recently ingested data sooner, improving the relevance and accuracy of search results and RAG responses for datasets that change frequently.

The 5-second default refresh interval is available in all 24 regions where Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is available today. To learn more, see the Amazon OpenSearch Serverless documentation.

items.title: AWS CloudFormation now simplifies stack update rollback operations
items.summary:
AWS CloudFormation now makes it simpler to complete an update rollback and get back to deploying. An update rollback returns your stack to a known good state. Starting today, if some resources cannot roll back automatically, force rollback enables you to complete the rollback in a single operation. It works across every CloudFormation workflow, from the AWS CLI, and SDKs to AWS CDK and AI agents.

With force rollback, CloudFormation completes the update rollback and returns your stack to a deployable state in a single operation, instead of requiring you to identify, list, and retry the operation for each affected resource. Any resource that still needs attention, such as one affected by a change outside CloudFormation, is recorded for you to review and resolve it before your next deployment.

To get started, run continue update rollback with the force rollback option, then create a drift-aware change set to review any configuration differences before your next deployment. To learn more, see  Continue rolling back an update  in the AWS CloudFormation User Guide.

Force rollback is available in all Regions at no additional cost. Refer to the  AWS Region table  for service availability details.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI announces training session APIs for serverless model customization
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports training session APIs, giving customers full control over their post-training algorithm without provisioning or managing GPU infrastructure. Managed techniques, including SFT, DPO, and other reinforcement learning methods, let customers pick a technique and a model and have SageMaker AI run the training. With training session APIs, teams get to write the training loop, whether that's reproducing SFT or DPO on their own terms or implementing a custom loss, a new RL reward signal, a data curriculum, or an algorithm straight from the latest research. Operations such as forward_backward(), optim_step(), and sample() become API calls against a live, stateful session, so customers compose whatever training procedure their technique requires while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, model and LoRA loading, distributed execution, fault recovery, checkpoint storage, and security.

Customers can call these operations directly from their own Python code to drive reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning, or custom training objectives against a live session, with checkpointing and resume built in. Billing is per token processed, so local computation like reward scoring isn't billed as GPU time. SageMaker AI is also releasing the SageMaker training sessions cookbook, a set of ready-to-run SFT and RL recipes customers can use as blueprints for their own training loops.

Training session APIs are generally available today in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Asia Pacific (Mumbai). To get started, install the SageMaker Python SDK and clone the cookbook, or launch a notebook in SageMaker Studio and connect a coding agent. To learn more, visit the documentation and the Amazon SageMaker AI webpage.

items.title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Bangalore, India
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced the expansion of 100 Gbps dedicated connections at the existing AWS Direct Connect location in the Netmagic DC2 data center near Bangalore, India. You can now establish private, direct network access to all public AWS Regions (except those in China), AWS GovCloud Regions, and AWS Local Zones from this location.

The Direct Connect service enables you to establish a private, physical network connection between AWS and your data center, office, or colocation environment. These private connections can provide a more consistent network experience than those made over the public internet.

For more information on the over 150 Direct Connect locations worldwide, visit the locations section of the Direct Connect product detail pages. Or, visit our getting started page to learn more about how to purchase and deploy Direct Connect.

items.title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports pausing and resuming connectors
items.summary:
Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now supports pausing and resuming connectors, letting you temporarily pause a connector from processing records and resume it later. This is useful when you need to stop data flow during maintenance on a source database or a sink target, or to pause processing while you investigate an upstream or downstream issue.

Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, pausing a connector meant deleting it and recreating it - a more disruptive operation, adding risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can pause a running connector and resume it in place when you are ready — a paused connector keeps its configuration, capacity settings, and committed offsets, and its tasks continue processing from the offsets they last committed when you resume.

This capability is available at no additional cost through the Amazon MSK Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDK, and AWS CDK in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is available. To learn more, visit the Amazon MSK Connect documentation. To get started, visit the Amazon MSK Console.

items.title: AWS announces AWS Interconnect - last mile preview with Megaport
items.summary:
AWS launches AWS Interconnect - last mile preview with Megaport, a fully managed connectivity offering that allows customers to connect their branch offices, data centers, and remote locations to AWS with just a few clicks, eliminating the friction and complexity of network setup. As a milestone collaboration between AWS and Megaport, AWS Interconnect - last mile combines AWS cloud innovation with Megaport operating one of the world's largest Software Defined Networks (SDN), with 1,200+ enabled data centers across 31 countries.

Through the AWS Management Console, customers can now instantly establish private, high-speed connections to AWS by simply choosing their preferred AWS Region, bandwidth speed, Direct Connect Gateway ID and partner subscriber ID. Once initiated, AWS generates an activation key to complete connectivity provisioning with Megaport. The launch simplifies the connectivity experience by pre-provisioning capacity and automating complex network configuration including BGP peering, VLAN configuration, and ASN assignment. At GA, customers will also be able to dynamically scale bandwidth from 1 Gbps to 100 Gbps through the AWS Console. The service is designed for high availability, with zero down-time maintenance, backed by a 99.99% SLA. 

AWS Interconnect - last mile is available in the San Jose (us-west-1) and N. Virginia (us-east-1) metros through Megaport. You can create a preview Interconnect using the AWS Management Console, Command Line Interface (CLI), or API. Partners can also easily adopt via a published open API package on GitHub. For more information, see the AWS Interconnect - last mile documentation and pricing pages.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports serverless model customization for Muse Glimmer, Qwen 3.8 and Ministral 3 models
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker AI now supports serverless model customization for Muse Glimmer, Qwen3.8 27B, and Ministral 3 3B, 8B, and 14B models. In addition to deploying these models on SageMaker AI, you can now adapt them to your specific domains and workflows, using supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) techniques. You can also adapt these models with either low-rank adaptation (LoRA) or full fine-tuning techniques. This launch adds these models to a wide variety of models available for serverless customization on SageMaker AI, including models from the Nova, Gemma 4, Nemotron 3.5, Qwen, Llama, gpt-oss, and DeepSeek families.

Model customization lets you tailor foundation models with your proprietary data so a smaller, right-sized model can match frontier-model quality on your tasks, while also reducing cost and latency. You can use labeled data with SFT to improve accuracy on domain-specific tasks, preference data with DPO to align outputs with your organization's tone, or reward signals with RFT to improve performance on new tasks. With serverless customization, SageMaker AI handles all infrastructure provisioning and training orchestration, so you can focus on your data and evaluation rather than cluster management, and only pay for what you use.

Serverless model customization on SageMaker AI is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To get started, navigate to the Models page in Amazon SageMaker Studio to launch a customization job, use the SageMaker Python SDK or use our Agent skills with your choice of coding assistant. To learn more and see the full supported list of models, see the Amazon SageMaker AI model customization documentation.

items.title: AgentCore Gateway now supports Bedrock InvokeModel APIs and model fallback
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway now supports the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream APIs on its inference endpoint, along with model fallback routing for inference traffic. With InvokeModel support, you can point your existing Amazon Bedrock SDK integration at the gateway and reach any model provider through one governed endpoint, without rewriting client code for each provider. With model fallback, the gateway automatically routes a request to an alternative model or provider when the primary destination is throttled, out of capacity, or unreachable, so your agents stay available without each client implementing its own retry logic.

For fallback routing, you define an ordered chain of alternative destinations in a gateway rule, along with the conditions that trigger a switch, such as throttling, server errors, or response timeouts. A built-in circuit breaker skips destinations that are currently failing, so requests reach a healthy destination faster and you avoid added latency for failed attempts. Fallback routing happens behind the scenes, which means you send one request and receive one response, regardless of the internal trial and error on a given request.

These features are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway is available (except those in China). To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway User Guide.

items.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 4 additional AWS regions
items.summary:
AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Thailand), and Europe (Spain). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 14 AWS Regions.

Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code.  Developers can use Lambda MicroVMs to give each user or job their own isolated compute environment without managing virtualization infrastructure or choosing between isolation, speed, and state retention. MicroVMs enable secure, stateful, and responsive code execution for applications including AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners.

With today's launch, developers can run Lambda MicroVMs closer to their end-users in 4 additional Regions, helping meet latency and data residency requirements. To get started, create a MicroVM image from your Dockerfile, then launch MicroVMs from that image. Give each user or job their own MicroVM with a dedicated HTTPS URL that supports popular connectivity protocols such as HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSockets. You can use MicroVMs through the AWS Lambda console, AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit, or with your preferred Agentic development tools using the Agent Toolkit for AWS.

To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda MicroVMs developer guide. For information on pricing, see Lambda MicroVMs pricing. Visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page for the latest region availability.

items.title: Amazon Quick Now Available in the AWS Singapore Region
items.summary:
Amazon Quick is now available in the AWS Asia Pacific (Singapore) region (ap-southeast-1). This launch allows customers in Singapore to access the full power of Amazon Quick while meeting local requirements for data sovereignty.

Amazon Quick provides business users an agentic teammate that quickly answers questions at work and turns those answers into actions. With Amazon Quick, every user is empowered to make better decisions faster and take actions without switching applications using AI they can trust. Today’s launch allows customers to take advantage of Amazon Quick’s capabilities including AI-powered chat, Research, Spaces, and QuickSight dashboards — with their data stored and processed locally within the AWS Singapore region. 

For a full list of AWS regions where Amazon Quick is available, visit the Quick regional availability page. To learn more, visit the Amazon Quick documentation or product detail page.

items.title: AWS Transform adds storage migration assessments for Amazon S3, EBS, EFS, and FSx
items.summary:
Migration assessments in AWS Transform now evaluate on-premises storage for migration to AWS. Instead of manually analyzing thousands of volumes across protocols, capacity, and performance, you upload a storage inventory and AWS Transform does the mapping for you. It matches each workload to the best-fit service, sizes the recommendation, and projects costs to produce a total cost of ownership business case. Bring NAS shares, SAN LUNs, direct-attached disks, or backup repositories via a NetApp Digital Advisor export, RVTools file, or other inventory. AWS Transform routes workloads across Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, Amazon EFS, and Amazon FSx (NetApp ONTAP, Windows File Server, OpenZFS, Lustre). Run what-if scenarios to compare deployment options such as Single-AZ vs. Multi-AZ or cost-optimized vs. performance-optimized, then ask follow-up questions about any result in chat.

Storage migration assessments are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is available. To learn more, see the AWS Transform User Guide.

items.title: AWS Service Reference Information now supports global condition keys, service names, and data plane classification
items.summary:
AWS is expanding programmatic service reference information to help you automate IAM policy management and keep your policies aligned with the latest service updates. The service reference now includes all aws:-prefixed global condition keys in a single machine-readable file, a ServiceName field mapping service identifiers to human-readable names, and an IsDataPlane property identifying which actions are data plane operations.

You can automate retrieval of this information to eliminate manual effort, and incorporate it directly into your existing policy management tools and processes. This feature is available at no additional cost. To get started, refer to the documentation on programmatic service reference information.

items.title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Manchester, England
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced the expansion of 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps dedicated connections with MACsec encryption capabilities at the existing AWS Direct Connect location in the Equinix MA3 data center near Manchester, England. You can now establish private, direct network access to all public AWS Regions (except those in China), AWS GovCloud Regions, and AWS Local Zones from this location. This is the third AWS Direct Connect location in England to provide 100 Gbps connections with MACsec encryption capabilities.

The Direct Connect service enables you to establish a private, physical network connection between AWS and your data center, office, or colocation environment. These private connections can provide a more consistent network experience than those made over the public internet.

For more information on the over 150 Direct Connect locations worldwide, visit the locations section of the Direct Connect product detail pages. Or, visit our getting started page to learn more about how to purchase and deploy Direct Connect.

items.title: Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS now support On-Demand Capacity Reservations
items.summary:
Starting today, you can reserve compute capacity for your Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS DB instances in one or more Availability Zones for as long as you need it. Reserving capacity helps ensure that DB instance create, restore, scale-compute, and start operations don't fail because of insufficient capacity.

On-Demand Capacity Reservations are designed for workloads that need assurance that specific DB instance capacity will be available when they need it for business-critical events, such as migrations, product launches, seasonal peaks, high-availability deployments, or disaster recovery. You choose the DB instance class, engine, Availability Zones, and reserved capacity per Availability Zone, and RDS holds that capacity for you. Capacity can be reserved in two or more Availability Zones to support Multi-AZ deployments. To use the reserved capacity, reference the reservation when you create, restore, modify, or start a DB instance.

You can reserve capacity for immediate use with no commitment and cancel at any time, or schedule a reservation to begin 5 to 120 days in the future with a minimum commitment. Reserved capacity is billed at On-Demand rates while the reservation is active, whether or not DB instances within the reservation are running. Discounts from your existing Reserved DB Instances or Database Savings Plans apply automatically.

On-Demand Capacity Reservations are available for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS in all AWS commercial Regions. To learn more about On-Demand Capacity Reservations, visit the documentation for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS.

items.title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate, in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region.

Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate between additional AWS Regions, helping you meet resilience, data residency, and compliance requirements in the Regions that best align with your business needs.

MRR is available as an add-on for user pools in the Essentials or Plus feature tiers, and requires a multi-Region AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK). For the full list of AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region. To get started, visit the developer guide for instructions and the pricing page for pricing details.

items.title: Beam model by Reflection is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and AWS Trainium
items.summary:
Beam, the first open weight model offered by US-based Reflection, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, the model hub in Amazon SageMaker AI. According to Beam, they operate at the frontier of open weight models in its class, with strong performance across reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks. Beam is for teams who build on and with an open weight model, not just call one. Customers who want to adapt a frontier model to their own domain can fine-tune it, inspect and modify its weights, and embed it deep in their agents and workflows, all while keeping full control of their data and infrastructure. Beam runs alongside other models that customers already use in SageMaker AI and scales to meet production demand with the same controls, audit trails, and monitoring built into every SageMaker AI deployment. Additionally, Beam was ported and optimized for AWS Trainium3, giving customers a high-performance, cost-efficient option for deploying and scaling the model from day one. “Reflection is delivering frontier AI that developers can actually control, not just rent through an API. Bringing Beam to SageMaker AI puts that capability in front of millions of developers on infrastructure they already trust, running in their own AWS account, on their own data, fully in their control," said Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO, Reflection.

Teams building on Beam can take it well beyond calling an API: fine-tune it on proprietary code and data, specialize it for their own domains, and wire it into multi-step agentic workflows across their tools. In practice that means resolving real software issues, generating and reviewing code, automating operations work, and tackling advanced math and science reasoning on a model they can shape rather than one they simply consume. Because Beam is released under the Apache 2.0 license, customers can inspect and customize the model, while also running it in their own AWS accounts, so data stays private and under their control, protected by the same AWS security and compliance capabilities they already rely on. “Advanced AI models like Beam, now available on Amazon SageMaker, let us run open weight frontier AI entirely inside our own secure environments, with full visibility into the weights, the data, and the pipeline. In the age of multi-model AI, the pairing of openness and managed infrastructure is an essential addition to the AI ecosystem. The freedom to deploy and adapt advanced AI, tailored to mission problems with client-specific security and controls, gives more agencies greater flexibility to deploy advanced AI across their enterprise,” said Garrett Berntsen, Chief AI Officer, Accenture Federal Services.

Beam is initially available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart in US East (N. Virginia) and US East (Ohio). The model is available in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 checkpoint variants, and can be deployed through a fully managed SageMaker JumpStart endpoint. To start, search for "Beam" in SageMaker JumpStart within Amazon SageMaker Studio, or deploy it directly on Sagemaker AI.  To learn more, read the AWS Machine Learning blog: Introducing Reflection Beam, SageMaker AI documentation and SageMaker JumpStart documentation for deployment guidance.

items.title: AWS Neuron 2.33 adds native PyTorch support, Neuron Observer, and other new features
items.summary:
AWS Neuron 2.33 is now available, introducing TorchNeuron, the native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium, in public beta. You can run models written with the standard PyTorch APIs on Amazon EC2 Trn2 and Trn3 instances, in eager mode or with torch.compile. This release also introduces Neuron Observer in public beta, which detects Trainium health issues in under a second and identifies the affected node or device.

The vLLM Neuron plugin upgrades to vLLM 0.29.0, and the vLLM Omni Neuron plugin for Wan2.2 video generation is now part of the Neuron release. Both support native PyTorch compilation through TorchNeuron. A new Neuron Deep Learning AMI and Deep Learning Container for PyTorch training include TorchNeuron, PyTorch 2.14, and TorchTitan. Neuron Explorer opens profiles captured with torch.profiler. From a PyTorch memory snapshot, it now attributes allocations to the Python source lines that made them, for debugging out-of-memory errors in eager mode.

Kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) can now use the full Python language for metaprogramming, including generators and class inheritance. The NKI Library adds 25 new experimental kernels, including kernels for DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen3.5, and Kimi Delta Attention.

To get started, see the following resources:

  • AWS Neuron 2.33.0 Release Notes

  • AWS TorchNeuron documentation

  • AWS Neuron Observer documentation

  • AWS Neuron Kernel Interface documentation

  • AWS Neuron

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer launches two new layouts for agent workspace
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now offers two different layouts that optimize screen space on the agent workspace. Contact center agents spend hours each day in the agent workspace, which includes all of the contact controls and applications they need to resolve customer issues. Agents who handle different channels and workflows want the workspace arranged differently, so that they can quickly read, respond, and access their tools. Now, administrators can choose the best layout for each team, maximizing agent efficiency and satisfaction.

On the Modern layout, contact controls are at the top of the workspace, maximizing screen space for the applications beneath during voice calls. When agents handle chat, email, and task contacts on the Modern layout, they now have a taller, wider area to read and respond. The Classic layout offers a familiar experience for agents already using the agent workspace, now with contact controls that expand and contract by channel and a resizable agent assist application. Administrators can assign the Modern layout to a team migrating from another agent desktop with controls at the top, while teams already familiar with the agent workspace can use the Classic layout.

You can use the new layouts for the Amazon Connect Customer agent workspace in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London).

To learn more and get started, see the agent workspace in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

items.title: Amazon S3 server access log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs now available in five additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon S3 server access log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and AWS China Regions. With your access logs in CloudWatch Logs, you can query them as they arrive, set alarms, and encrypt them with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. This new delivery path complements the existing delivery of server access logs to S3 general purpose buckets, giving you more flexibility in how you monitor and analyze access to your data.

With delivery to CloudWatch Logs, you can set alarms on error rates, monitor traffic patterns, investigate access incidents, and correlate S3 access activity with the rest of your operational data.

S3 server access log delivery to CloudWatch Logs is now available in all AWS Regions. Amazon CloudWatch Logs charges for vended logs apply. For pricing details, visit Amazon CloudWatch pricing. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 User Guide.

items.title: AWS Network Firewall now supports Route 53 Resolved IP Validation
items.summary:
AWS Network Firewall now supports IP validation, extending domain-based filtering beyond HTTP/HTTPS to protocols such as SFTP and SSH. This new capability validates that a connection's destination IP address was resolved through your VPC's Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver, closing security gaps where clients could bypass domain rules.

This feature enables Network Firewall customers to implement domain filtering rules for any protocol, not just HTTP/HTTPS, providing more flexible security policies than IP-based rules alone. It simplifies protection against Server Name Identifier (SNI) spoofing by validating the IPs resolved by the Route 53 VPC Resolver against the SNI, ensuring traffic only reaches legitimately resolved destinations. Organizations can now enforce consistent domain-based security policies across all outbound traffic types, from web applications to file transfer protocols, without complex workarounds. Additionally, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall can be used with your VPC Resolver for extended DNS security.

Resolved IP validation is available in all AWS commercial regions where AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall are available, at no additional charge. For a full list of supported regions, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page.

To learn more, visit AWS Network Firewall product page and service documentation.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports custom sequence lengths for serverless model customization jobs
items.summary:
Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces the ability to configure the sequence length used during your serverless model customization job. Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization supports fine-tuning for many open-weight models, including models from popular families including gpt-oss, Gemma, Llama, Nemotron, and Qwen. Previously, each fine-tuning recipe ran at a fixed sequence length that customers could not modify. Customers sometimes need to modify these parameters to achieve better results for their use case. Customers also asked for longer sequence lengths than the static defaults we supported on some models.

Now, you can set sequence length parameters as part of the customization job's hyperparameters, anywhere up to the published maximum for your chosen model and technique. You can set the dataset_max_len hyperparameter for SFT and DPO jobs or set max_prompt_length and max_response_length hyperparameters for RFT jobs. This gives you more control to match your training data characteristics, whether you are working with short question-answer pairs or multi-page documents. Published maximums are up to 16K tokens for many models depending on model and technique.

Serverless model customization on SageMaker AI is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To get started, navigate to the Models page in Amazon SageMaker Studio to launch a customization job, use the SageMaker Python SDK or use our Agent skills with your choice of coding assistant. To learn more, and see the list of models and supported sequence lengths per technique, see the SageMaker AI documentation.

items.title: AWS Transform now builds new networks and modernizes security groups
items.summary:
AWS Transform for migrations now gives you three ways to bring your network to AWS. In addition to migrating and modernizing your existing network, you can build a new network from scratch or convert your on-premises access rules into optimized security groups and deploy them into existing VPCs. Whichever path you choose, you arrive on AWS with a secure and scalable network foundation.

On-premises networks accumulate years of definitions and access rules that you may not want to carry to AWS as-is. For a clean start, AWS Transform builds a new network aligned to AWS best practices. To bring your access rules with you, AWS Transform converts them into security groups and modernizes them as it goes, detecting stale rules and recommending optimizations, then deploys the groups into your existing VPCs without redeploying your network stack.

These capabilities allow you migrate to any AWS commercial or GovCloud Region.

To get started, see Migrate networks. To learn more, visit AWS Transform for migrations.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore を使用した電力・公益事業向けのインテリジェントなアラーム管理
items.summary: 北米の大手電力会社が Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 上で運用しているマルチエージェント AI アーキテクチャを紹介します。このアーキテクチャにより、オペレーターがシフトごとに何十回も、複数のシステムをまたいで手作業で行っていた調査が不要になり、アラームのトリアージにかかる時間が数時間から数分に短縮されています。業界の課題、マルチエージェントの設計、GitHub 上のリファレンス実装について説明します。

items.title: スペックファースト: SAP ABAP のスペック駆動開発
items.summary: AI コーディングエージェントで ABAP を生成する際、スペックがなければ開発上の判断が記録に残りません。本記事では、Kiro CLI 上で動作する AWS Coding Plugin for SAP ABAP を使ったスペック駆動開発 (SDD) の進め方を紹介します。良い ABAP スペックの書き方、AI-DLC に沿ったスペックからトランスポートリリースまでの流れ、ステアリングファイルによるチーム標準の適用を解説します。スペックを Git に残すことで、ドキュメントのない既存プログラムにも変更のたびに最新の仕様が蓄積されます。

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 が Kiro で利用可能になりました
items.summary: Claude Haiku 5.5 が本日より Kiro IDE、CLI、Web、Crew のすべてで利用可能になりました。Claude 5.5 ファミリーで最も高速なモデルで、大量に実行され素早い応答が求められる作業を想定しています。Claude Haiku 4.5 から明確に進化しました。Haiku 5.5 の登場で、Claude 5.5 の 3 つのモデルがすべて Kiro で使えるようになります。最も難しい問題には Opus 5.5、日常的なコーディングには Sonnet 5.5 があり、処理量や速度が何より重要な場面では Haiku 5.5 が担います。

items.title: AWS Coding Plugin for SAP ABAP, powered by Kiro のご紹介
items.summary: Kiro を搭載した AWS Coding Plugin for SAP ABAP をリリースしました。SAP の ABAP Development Tools (ADT) と併せて Eclipse 上でスペック駆動開発 (SDD) を実現し、開発者とエージェントが協働して要件定義・設計・実装を進められます。IBM Consulting では、カスタム ABAP 拡張の開発時間を最大 30% 短縮し、開発後の不具合を最大 45% 削減しました。ECC から S/4HANA、BTP ABAP まで幅広いシステムに対応し、クリーンコアと RISE への移行を加速します。

items.title: 週刊生成AI with AWS – 2026/10/19 週
items.summary: 今週の「週刊生成 AI with AWS」は、NEC 様の Claude Code 全社展開（約 3 万人体制を目指す CoE・チャンピオン制度）と、コーテッグ様が Amazon Bedrock AgentCore で構築した AI 分析基盤「Dotta」の 2 つの国内事例や、Amazon Bedrock の API キー保護や最小権限、AI コーディングエージェント向けコントロールフレームワークなどセキュリティ関連のブログに加え、AWS Physical AI Toolchain、AWS DevOps Agent の調査コスト制御も取り上げています。 サービスアップデートでは、Amazon Bedrock での Claude 構造化出力、Amazon CloudWatch Omni の東京リージョン対応、Kiro IDE と CLI のメモリ機能など 25 件を紹介しています。
